When an mRNA vaccine is injected into the body, it enters the cells near the injection site. The mRNA contains instructions for making a specific viral protein, such as the spike protein of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Once inside the cell, the mRNA is used by the cell's machinery to produce the viral protein. The protein is then displayed on the surface of the cell, which alerts the immune system. The immune system recognizes the protein as foreign and mounts an immune response, producing antibodies and activating T cells. This immune response helps the body recognize and fight the actual virus if it is encountered in the future. Memory cells are created during this process, which provide long-term immunity. The mRNA is eventually broken down and cleared from the body.
